card.name: Modifiers before landscape and heritage nouns
card.fires_on: Adjectives or linking words like stone, rock, old, abandoned or as, just before a noun for an outdoor feature or human-made object. The setting is land, archaeology or habitat text in general web writing.

modes.label: Stone/rock as modifier
modes.description: The word stone or rock sits before a noun like posts, tools, paintings or forts.
modes.example: several<< stone>> posts or stoops were erected to guide

modes.label: Old or abandoned before land features
modes.description: An adjective such as old or abandoned comes before fields, mines or crosses.
modes.example: In trees of moist woods or along fence rows in<< old>> fields.

modes.label: Linking words in lists of land features
modes.description: A comma or small word precedes the next item in a list of outdoor facilities or settlement features.
modes.example: installation and maintenance of parking lots<<,>> roads, trails, boat access facilities,

card.writes: It pushes toward words about settlements and places, and away from tree and forest words.
card.plain: It fires on words like stone or old that come right before a place or landscape noun, where the next word is not likely to be tree.
